output.answer: Section 4 imposes income tax on the taxable income of every person who has taxable income for the tax year, and the tax is levied at the rate or rates specified in Division I or Division II of Part I of the First Schedule, as applicable (tax year 2027).

The surcharge under section 4AB is levied at a rate of ten percent of the income tax payable[1]. It applies to individuals and associations of persons whose taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million, except that no surcharge is payable on income chargeable under the head “Salary”[1].
For tax year 2027, a banking company whose income exceeds Rs. 150 million is subject to a super tax of 10 % of that income.

The super tax rate is 8% of the income for a person (who is not a banking company, a fertilizer seller, or a Fifth‑Schedule person) whose income exceeds Rs. 500 million (Division IIB, Table, tax year 2027 onwards).

For tax year 2027, section 7B does not apply when the profit on debt exceeds Rs 5 million, as the provision expressly excludes such amounts. Consequently, no separate tax under section 7B is levied on profit on debt that is above the five‑million‑rupee threshold.[1]
The heads of income are Salary, Income from Property, Income from Business, Capital Gains and Income from Other Sources (tax year 2027 onwards).

Yes, overtime payments and bonuses are included in salary for income‑tax purposes; Section 12 of the Income Tax Ordinance lists overtime payment and bonus among the amounts that constitute salary and are chargeable under the head “Salary”.

For tax year 2027, a motor vehicle provided by an employer for an employee’s private use is treated as a taxable perquisite under the head “Salary” and its value must be included in the employee’s income as prescribed.  The valuation is prescribed in Rule 5 of the Income‑Tax Rules 2002, which sets the taxable amount at 5 % of the employer’s cost (or fair market value if leased) for partial private use and 10 % of the cost (or FMV) for full private use【1】【2】

Under section 15, “rent” means any amount received or receivable by the owner of land or a building as consideration for the use or occupation of, or the right to use or occupy, that land or building, and it also includes any forfeited deposit paid under a contract for the sale of land or a building [1]. The definition is reiterated in the definitions section of the Ordinance, which states that “rent” means rent as defined in sub‑section (2) of section 15 and includes an amount treated as rent under section 16 [2]. Additionally, any amount included in rent for the provision of amenities, utilities or other services connected with the renting of the building is also chargeable to tax, though under the head “Income from Other Sources” [1].
Agricultural income is exempt from tax under the federal Income Tax Ordinance for the tax year 2027 onward.
No, a scholarship received to meet the cost of your education is exempt from tax for tax year 2027, unless the scholarship is paid directly or indirectly by an associate.
Support money received by a spouse under an agreement to live apart is exempt from tax for tax year 2027.

For tax year 2027, a short‑term resident individual’s foreign‑source income is exempt if the person is resident in Pakistan solely because of employment and has been present in Pakistan for periods not exceeding three years, provided the income is not from a business established in Pakistan and is not brought into or received in Pakistan. [1]

For the tax year 2027, an unabsorbed business loss can be carried forward for up to six tax years immediately succeeding the year in which the loss was first computed, unless a specific provision applies (e.g., ten years for certain government‑owned banks, eight years for resident hotel companies, etc.).

You may claim a deduction for Zakat that you have actually paid in the tax year, as provided in Section 60 and also under Section 40 for profit‑on‑debt income. However, any portion of the Zakat allowance that cannot be used as a deduction in that year cannot be refunded, carried forward to a later year, or carried back to an earlier year.[1,3]

For tax year 2027, any individual whose taxable income is less than Rs 1.5 million may claim a deductible allowance for tuition fees paid for his/her children; the allowance can be applied against the tax liability of either parent who actually made the payment and provided the NTN or the institution’s name. The amount allowed is the lesser of (a) 5 % of the total tuition fees paid, (b) 25 % of the individual’s taxable income, or (c) Rs 60,000 multiplied by the number of children [1].

Yes. Under Section 60A of the Income Tax Ordinance a person is entitled to a deductible allowance for any Workers’ Welfare Fund paid by the person in the tax year, except where the amount is paid to a province by a trans‑provincial establishment.

Yes, a donation to a public university qualifies for a tax credit under Section 61 of the Income Tax Ordinance, provided the donation is made by crossed cheque and the credit is calculated as the lesser of the total donation (or its FMV) and 30 % of your taxable income (for an individual) or 20 % (for a company) for the tax year 2027.

An eligible person (as defined in sub‑section 19A of section 2) who derives income chargeable to tax under the head “Salary” or the head “Income from Business” is entitled to a tax credit for any contribution or premium paid in the year to an approved pension fund under the Voluntary Pension System Rules [1].

Yes. Under Section 63A of the Income Tax Ordinance, an individual can claim a tax credit for the profit on debt (interest) paid on a low‑cost housing loan used to construct or acquire a personal house, calculated by the formula (A/B) × C and limited to the lesser of the actual profit paid or 30 % of taxable income; profit deductible under Section 15A is excluded. This applies for tax year 2027 onward.

Under the Income Tax Ordinance, a "tax year" is a twelve‑month period ending on 30 June and is normally identified by the calendar year in which that date falls (the “normal tax year”) [1]. A person may be permitted to use a different twelve‑month period as a “special tax year” if the Commissioner approves an application, and such special year is also denoted by the calendar year in which its closing date falls [1]. The definition of “tax year” in the Ordinance’s definitions section refers back to this provision in section 74 [3].

An individual must be present in Pakistan for at least one hundred and eighty‑three days in aggregate during the tax year to be deemed a resident individual [1]. For this purpose, any part of a day in which the individual is present (including arrival and departure days) is counted as a full day, except days spent in transit, as per Rule 14 of the Income Tax Rules [2].

Yes. Under Section 82 an individual is a resident if he is present in Pakistan for a total of 183 days or more in the tax year, or if he is a federal or provincial employee posted abroad, provided he does not stay in any other country for more than 182 days and is not a resident taxpayer elsewhere. Rule 14 explains that any part of a day in Pakistan (including arrival and departure days and public holidays, leave, strike days, etc.) counts as a full day for this purpose. Thus a Pakistani citizen who spends much of the year abroad can still be a resident individual if he meets the 183‑day presence test or qualifies under the government‑posted‑abroad exception.

A company is treated as a resident company for a tax year if it satisfies any one of the following conditions: (a) it is incorporated or formed under any law in force in Pakistan; (b) the control and management of its affairs are wholly situated in Pakistan at any time during the year; or (c) it is a Provincial or Local Government in Pakistan. This definition applies for tax year 2027 onward.[1,3]

For tax year 2027, a resident individual’s foreign‑source salary is exempt from Pakistani tax provided the individual has paid foreign income tax on that salary, such as tax withheld by the employer and remitted to the foreign revenue authority. Hence, if foreign tax has already been paid, the salary is not taxed in Pakistan.[2]

For tax year 2027 the foreign tax credit on foreign‑source income is limited to the lesser of (a) the foreign income tax actually paid (including foreign withholding tax) or (b) the Pakistan tax that would be payable on that income, which is calculated by applying the taxpayer’s average Pakistan tax rate for the year to the net foreign‑source income. The credit is applied head‑by‑head and cannot exceed the Pakistan tax liability on that head of income.

For tax year 2027, salary is Pakistan‑source income if it is received from any employment exercised in Pakistan, wherever it is paid, or if it is paid by, or on behalf of, the Federal Government, a Provincial Government or a Local Government in Pakistan, wherever the employment is exercised.[1]

If you cannot explain the nature and source of an investment, money, valuable article or the funds used for an expenditure, the amount will be deemed unexplained and must be included in your taxable income. The unexplained amount is added to income from Other Sources, or if it relates to suppressed production, sales or receipts, to income from Business, in the tax year to which it relates if the asset is situated in Pakistan or is Pakistan‑source, or in the preceding tax year if it is foreign‑source and discovered later [1]. The Commissioner may also include any shortfall between the declared cost and a reasonable cost of the investment or expenditure as income from Other Sources [2]. An exception applies where foreign exchange up to Rs 5 million is remitted through normal banking channels and a bank certificate is produced; such amounts are not subject to the provisions of section 111 [2].

For tax year 2027, section 113 applies to a resident company, a permanent establishment of a non‑resident company, an individual whose turnover is Rs 100 million or more in the tax year, and an association of persons whose turnover is Rs 100 million or more in the tax year, where the tax payable is nil or less than the minimum tax percentage of turnover specified in the First Schedule.[1]

For tax year 2027, a return of income must be furnished by (a) every company; (ab) every non‑company person whose taxable income exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to tax; (ac) any non‑profit organization as defined in the Ordinance; (ae) every person whose income is subject to final taxation; (b) any person not covered by the foregoing who (i) has been taxed in either of the two preceding years, (ii) claims a loss carry‑forward, (iii) owns immovable property of at least 500 sq yds or a flat in specified municipal areas, (iv) owns immovable property of at least 500 sq yds in a rating area, (v) owns a flat of at least 2,000 sq ft in a rating area, (vi) owns a motor vehicle with engine capacity above 1,000 cc, (vii) has obtained a National Tax Number, (viii) holds a commercial/industrial electricity connection with annual bill over Rs 500,000, (ix) is a resident registered with a chamber of commerce, professional body or similar, or (x) is a resident individual required to file a foreign income and assets statement; (c) any persons or classes notified by the Board with the Minister’s approval; and (1A) every individual whose business income is between Rs 300,000 and Rs 400,000. [1]

For tax year 2027, a widow is exempt from filing a return of income solely because she owns immovable property such as a 500‑square‑yard house. Section 115 expressly lists a widow among persons not required to furnish a return for reasons covered by sub‑clauses (iii)‑(vi) of clause (b) of section 114, which include ownership of immovable property of 500 sq yds or more.[1][2]

The Commissioner, by written notice, may require an individual to submit a wealth statement in the prescribed form and verified manner that includes: (a) the person’s total assets and liabilities, including foreign assets and liabilities; (b) the total assets and liabilities of the person’s spouse (if dependent), minor children and other dependents; (c) any assets transferred by the person to another person during the period specified and the consideration received; (d) the total expenditures incurred by the person, spouse, minor children and other dependents during the period specified and details of those expenditures; and (e) a reconciliation statement of wealth. [1]
A salaried individual must file the income‑tax return on or before the 30th day of September following the end of the tax year.

You may apply in writing to the Commissioner for an extension before the return’s due date, stating a reasonable cause such as absence from Pakistan, sickness or any other reasonable reason. The Commissioner can grant an extension of up to fifteen days, and longer periods only in exceptional circumstances. The extension does not alter the due date for payment of the tax itself.[1]

For tax year 2027 the Commissioner may amend an original assessment order only within five years from the end of the financial year in which the original assessment was issued or treated as issued [1]. If the assessment has already been amended, a further amendment is permitted within the later of (a) five years from the end of the financial year of the original assessment, or (b) one year from the end of the financial year in which the amended assessment was issued [1,4].
The appeal must be filed within thirty days of receiving the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) [1].
Income tax on your taxable income is payable on the due date for filing your return of income for the tax year (2027) as specified by the Federal Government.[1]

No, income that is subject to salary withholding under section 149 is excluded from the calculation of quarterly advance tax under section 147; such income is listed among the exemptions in sub‑section (1)(b) of section 147. This applies for tax year 2027.

Yes. Under Section 149(1A) a pension paid to a former employee who is under 70 years and exceeds Rs 10 million is subject to tax deducted on the amount above Rs 10 million at the rate in Division I of Part I of the First Schedule; the same rule is reflected in Section 12(2A)(i) which treats such pension as a final tax at those rates, while a pension received by a person aged 70 years or more is not taxed. (Tax year 2027)

Under section 151, the entity that makes the payment of profit on debt – i.e., the payer – must deduct the withholding tax. This includes (a) the person paying yield on a National Savings or Post Office Savings account, (b) a banking company or financial institution paying profit on a debt account or deposit, (c) the Federal, Provincial or Local Government paying profit on a security, (d) a banking company, financial institution or finance society paying profit on bonds, certificates, debentures or similar instruments, and (e) any special‑purpose vehicle or company paying a return on investment in sukuk (sub‑section 1A).[1]

When a resident pays a royalty or a fee for technical services to a non‑resident, the payer must deduct tax at source from the gross amount at the rate prescribed in Division IV of Part I of the First Schedule, which is 15 % of the gross royalty or fee for technical services (10 % applies only to other payments) [1, 2, 4]. The tax is withheld at the time of payment and remitted to the tax authorities for the tax year 2027 onward.
Payments for services are exempt from withholding under section 153 when the total amount paid to the service provider is less than Rs 30,000 in aggregate during a financial year.

For the tax year 2027, the withholding tax on export proceeds of IT services (including computer software and IT‑enabled services) by an exporter registered and certified with the Pakistan Software Export Board is 0.25 % of the proceeds. This rate is specified in Division IVA of Part III of the First Schedule under section 154A.
For tax year 2027, if the exporter is not registered with the Pakistan Software Export Board, the withholding tax deducted on export of services proceeds is 1% of the proceeds.
For tax year 2027, the tenant must withhold Rs.10,000 (5% of the amount exceeding Rs.300,000, i.e., 5% × Rs.200,000) from the Rs.500,000 rent paid to the individual landlord.
For prize bond winnings the payer must deduct 15% of the gross amount paid as withholding tax, and this tax is final under section 156(3). This applies for tax year 2027.
The withholding tax rate on winnings from a lottery, raffle or quiz is 20% of the gross amount paid for tax year 2027.

To stop withholding tax on payments that are exempt or subject to a lower rate, you must obtain an exemption or lower‑rate certificate under section 159.  Submit a written application in the prescribed form (or online for non‑residents under rule 40FA) together with the required information, documents and affidavits, and ensure you have filed all returns and are not in default of any tax liability [1,2].  The Commissioner will issue the certificate within fifteen days for a company (or deem it issued after fifteen days) and, once issued, the payer must follow the certificate and refrain from deducting tax under Division II or III [1,3].

If a withholding agent fails to deduct tax, the agent becomes personally liable to pay the tax to the Commissioner and may be ordered to recover it from the person from whom the tax should have been collected (Section 161 and Section 162) [5,4]. The agent is also subject to a penalty of Rs 40,000 or an amount equal to the tax involved, whichever is higher, under the offences and penalties provisions (Section 182) [6]. The agent must be given an opportunity of being heard before recovery is made (Section 161(1A)).

Yes. Under the Tenth Schedule, tax deducted or collected at source may be adjusted against the tax payable in the return filed for the relevant tax year, provided the return is filed before provisional assessment or under the specified sub‑rule.[2] This adjustment applies for the tax year 2027 onward.[4]

Under section 169, a tax that is deducted or collected as a "final tax" means the amount is treated as the full tax liability on that income and is not included in the computation of taxable income (the income is not chargeable under any head) [1]. No deductions, allowances, loss set‑offs or tax credits may be applied to reduce the tax, and the tax cannot be refunded unless the amount deducted exceeds the tax due [1].
For tax year 2027, the Commissioner must decide a refund application within sixty days of receiving it and issue a written order of the decision.
A taxpayer must keep accounts and records for six years after the end of the tax year to which they relate.

No. Under Section 181(1A) of the Income Tax Ordinance, an online marketplace may not allow any vendor to use its platform for e‑commerce transactions unless the vendor is registered under the Ordinance. This makes it mandatory for all vendors to be registered before they can sell on the platform (tax year 2027).

Yes, an individual who files the return after the due date can be included in the Active Taxpayers' List, but only if he pays the surcharge of Rs 25,000 as prescribed in the proviso to section 182A(1).

A non‑resident taxpayer (or non‑resident person) may apply in writing for an advance ruling under section 206A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. This is the only category expressly permitted to make the application.[1,2]

Yes. Under section 236, advance tax must be collected on the internet bill of a subscriber and on prepaid internet cards (section 236). The rate is 15 % of the amount of the bill or the sale price of the prepaid internet card (Division V, Part IV of the First Schedule) for tax year 2027.
The buyer must pay advance tax equal to 1.25 % of the fair market value of the immovable property at the time of registration, recording or attestation of the transfer.

Yes. When you pay a foreign merchant using a credit, debit or prepaid card, the banking company must deduct advance tax at the rate of 0.5% of the gross amount remitted abroad, as prescribed under section 236Y and Division XXVII of the First Schedule.
For immovable property disposed of within one year of acquisition, the capital gains tax rate is 15% (applicable to all taxpayers, including those on the Active Taxpayers’ List) for tax year 2027.

For listed shares acquired on or after 1 July 2024 and disposed of by a person who is on the Active Taxpayers’ List, the capital gains tax rate is 15 % when the holding period does not exceed one year (the rate is specified for ATL persons in the table for that acquisition period).

نہیں، وفاقی انکم ٹیکس قانون کے تحت زرعی آمدن ٹیکس سے مستثنیٰ ہے۔ اس کی وضاحت سیکشن 41 میں کی گئی ہے کہ زرعی آمدن کو اس آرڈیننس کے تحت ٹیکس سے آزاد قرار دیا گیا ہے (tax year 2027)۔

عام طور پر، سیکشن 57 کے تحت کاروباری نقصان کو زیادہ سے زیادہ چھ (6) مسلسل ٹیکس سالوں تک آگے لے جایا جا سکتا ہے[1]۔ تاہم، مخصوص حالات میں یہ مدت بڑھائی جاتی ہے: وفاقی حکومت کی ملکیتی بینک کے لیے دس (10) سال، ہوٹل کاروبار کے لیے آٹھ (8) سال، اور پاکستان انٹرنیشنل ایئرلائنز کے لیے بھی دس (10) سال[1]۔

ٹیکس سال 2027 کے لیے، ادا کی گئی زکوٰۃ پر سیکشن 60 کے تحت ٹیکس میں کٹوتی ملتی ہے[1]۔ تاہم، اس کٹوتی کا کوئی حصہ جو اس سال استعمال نہ ہو سکے، اسے اگلے سال منتقل نہیں کیا جا سکتا؛ نہ تو ریفنڈ ملے گا اور نہ ہی کیری‑فارورڈ کی اجازت ہے[1]۔

output.answer: Section 4 imposes income tax on the taxable income of every person who has taxable income for the tax year. The tax is levied at the rate or rates specified in Division I or Division II of Part I of the First Schedule, as applicable to the taxpayer, for tax year 2027 onward.

For tax year 2027 onwards, the surcharge under Section 4AB is levied at a rate of ten percent of the income tax imposed under Division I of Part I of the First Schedule [1]. It applies only when an individual’s or association’s taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million, and no surcharge is payable on income chargeable under the head “Salary” [1].
For tax year 2027, a banking company whose income exceeds Rs 150 million is subject to a super tax of 10 % of that income.

For tax year 2027, a person who is not a banking company, not a fertilizer seller and not a Fifth‑Schedule person and whose income exceeds Rs 500 million is subject to a super tax of 8 % of that income.[1]
